faq.q: What does an AI product photo generator make?
faq.a: A listing image, a room scene, a close-up of one detail, or a square ad. You start from one clear photo or a short description. You review the file before you publish.

faq.q: How do I make the photo from one product picture?
faq.a: Upload a product photo or describe the scene, choose the style, then make a square image. You see how many credits it will use before you start.

faq.q: Is there a free AI product photo generator plan?
faq.a: No. There is no free plan. Each image uses 24 credits, the units your plan spends. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Are the photos usable on a product page?
faq.a: Yes, for a listing image, a room scene, and an ad image. Check each result against the product you ship so the color, shape, and details still match.

faq.q: Can I make a white background and a room scene?
faq.a: Yes. A clean listing and a room scene are separate photos, and each one uses 24 credits. Check the product in both before you publish.

faq.q: Do these photos replace a studio shoot?
faq.a: They take the place of the studio booking for a new scene. You still compare the file with the product you ship. Add prices in your own editor after download.

faq.q: Can I use the downloads on my store?
faq.a: Downloads have no stamped logo. You can use them on your store and in ads, under our terms. You still need the rights to the photo you upload. The notes in [AI product photography](page:blog-ai-product-photography-guide) explain that check.

faq.q: Can I add a price or a logo on the photo?
faq.a: Add prices, sale offers, and logo text in your editor after download. Words the tool writes on the photo can be wrong. [Shopify product photos](page:plat-shopify) shows one place those files can go.

faq.q: Where are the AI product photo templates?
faq.a: Browse [product ad templates](page:templates) for plain product photos, lifestyle scenes (photos set in a room), and ad layouts. Then upload your product photo here and describe the scene.

faq.q: Can I make a batch, or connect my store software (an API)?
faq.a: Yes. A batch makes several scenes from the photos you upload. An API is a connection that lets your store software send the photos. Each photo still uses 24 credits, shown before you start.

faq.q: Can I turn the photo into a video with a voiceover?
faq.a: Yes. Turn that photo into a product video. Then add a spoken voice, on-screen captions, or a song from the music library. A 6-second clip uses 24 credits. A 10-second clip uses 40, a 15-second clip uses 60, and a 30-second clip uses 120. [Image to video](page:image-to-video) is that next step.

items.d: Upload the product photo and make the scene. Then trim the short video in the built-in editor, so you do not need another app.

items.t: Show a generated person holding the product
items.d: Use the photo so the product stays the same. A generated adult can hold it in a short video from [image to video](page:image-to-video). That person is not a real customer.

items.t: Pick a generated actor for the clip
items.d: Choose a look from the [actor library](page:ai-actors), a set of generated people. Then keep the same person on the next version of the ad.

items.t: Make the same ad in more than one language
items.d: Write the script, then make the spoken version in the languages your shoppers use. Check the words before you publish.

items.t: See the credit cost before you start

items.t: Use a generated presenter instead of a filming day
items.d: The actor is generated. Do not present the clip as a real customer or a celebrity.

items.t: Reuse one generated person from photos you have
items.d: Upload a few clear photos and reuse that generated person on the next scene. A presenter for the ad starts on [spokesperson videos](page:spokesperson-videos).

items.t: Start from a product link, then publish the ad
items.d: Paste a [product link](page:url-to-video) and the tool drafts a script. Then pick an actor and make a video. Publish that file to [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok) or [Facebook](page:plat-facebook) from the editor.
